test_title: PYST 10: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Judicial review is essential to:

options.text: uphold the supremacy of the Constitution

solution:
The correct answer is __**uphold the supremacy of the Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Judicial review is a mechanism to ensure that laws and executive actions comply with the provisions of the Constitution, thereby upholding its supremacy.
 
• It empowers the judiciary to invalidate laws or actions by the legislature and executive if they violate constitutional principles.
 
• The concept of judicial review is derived from the principle of the separation of powers and checks and balances in governance.
 
• Judicial review safeguards fundamental rights and ensures accountability of the government to constitutional norms.
 
• This principle is integral to democratic governance and prevents arbitrary use of power by any branch of the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review:**

 
 
• The term refers to the authority of the courts to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts and executive decisions.
 
• Judicial review originated in the United States through the landmark case **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**.
 
• In India, judicial review is an essential feature of the Constitution under Articles **13, 32, and 226**.
 
• It is a part of the basic structure doctrine established by the Supreme Court in the **Keshavananda Bharati case (1973)**.
 
 
 
• **Supremacy of the Constitution:**
 
 
• The Constitution is the highest legal authority in India, and all laws and actions must conform to it.
 
• Article 141 ensures that judgments of the Supreme Court are binding on all courts in India.
 
• The concept reinforces the rule of law and prevents autocratic governance.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• It is a governance principle dividing powers among the legislature, executive, and judiciary.
 
• Judicial review acts as a check on the legislature and executive to maintain balance.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Judicial review ensures protection against violations of fundamental rights enshrined under Part III of the Constitution.
 
• Examples include the right to equality, freedom of speech, and protection against discrimination.
